answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so voting influence depends on paths reaching independently established nodes rather than on self-created identities. A Sybil cluster with few links to the honest network is a hollow region behind a low-conductance cut; min-cut and mixing bounds limit how much walk probability, and thus aggregate voting weight, can cross its ridge. Even a large basalt-like cluster cannot gain weight merely by adding internal attestations.
